summary: This is a Mol Labs public research discussion card (L15) proposing an assumption-kill experiment to test whether DunedinPACE slowing without concurrent GrimAge improvement fails to predict Oh plasma proteomic brain and immune organ-age benefit on the CALERIE phase-2 caloric restriction arm. The document is a hypothesis/proposal at TRL 1–2, with no new experimental data generated; it synthesizes existing literature (CALERIE RCT, Oh organ-age proteomics) and identifies a matched head-to-head multi-clock × organ-age panel as currently UNKNOWN. The predicted outcome is negative (DunedinPACE-alone does not predict organ-age benefit when GrimAge is flat).

content_blocks.title: Claim and Research Question
content_blocks.content: The central claim (L15) is: On the CALERIE phase-2 caloric-restriction (CR) arm, DunedinPACE slowing without concurrent GrimAge improvement fails to predict Oh plasma proteomic brain+immune organ-age benefit. Pre-registered Δ organ-age_brain and Δ organ-age_immune among DunedinPACE improvers with GrimAge inside a flat band are predicted to fall inside a null-benefit band. This is framed as an 'assumption-kill' of the claim that 'DunedinPACE-alone predicts organ-age benefit when GrimAge is flat.' Status: PREDICTION (not yet run). Execution status: NOT_RUN.

content_blocks.title: Why It Matters / Scientific Rationale
content_blocks.content: Longevity trial and consumer framing often treat DunedinPACE slowing as a stand-alone success signal even when GrimAge is flat. L15 is distinct from L4 (clock Δ without VO₂/muscle/organ-age as insufficient healthspan endpoint): L15 specifically addresses within-DNAm discordance (DunedinPACE− / GrimAge flat) adjudicated by an Oh proteomic brain+immune organ-age referee. CALERIE already shows within-DNAm discordance without Oh organ-age; Oh organ ages do not co-index DunedinPACE/GrimAge in PubMed overlap.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch / Experimental Design
content_blocks.content: Proposed method: Multi-clock-discordance analysis on the CALERIE phase-2 CR arm. Steps: (1) Stratify subjects with verified DunedinPACE improvement by whether GrimAge co-moves. (2) Score Oh plasma proteomic brain and immune organ-age Δ as secondary overlay/co-measure on the same arm. (3) Prefer secondary analysis of existing public trial arm (DNAm clocks on-arm; Oh organ ages overlay) before new wet assay or animal/human dosing. Key construct distinctions: DunedinPACE = blood DNAm pace-of-aging algorithm; GrimAge = blood DNAm lifespan/healthspan composite (DNAm surrogates of plasma proteins + smoking pack-years); Oh organ ages = plasma proteomic organ-of-origin models — fundamentally different constructs from blood DNAm. Method type: propose-assay.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Anchors
content_blocks.content:
Four key literature anchors cited:
1. PMID 35029144 (Belsky 2022, eLife, DOI 10.7554/eLife.73420): DunedinPACE blood DNAm pace-of-aging biomarker; associates with morbidity/disability/mortality; intervention-responsive. Not an Oh organ-age referee.
2. PMID 30669119 (Lu 2019, Aging, DOI 10.18632/aging.101684): DNAm GrimAge predicts lifespan/healthspan and incident disease. GrimAge co-movement axis; flat GrimAge is the within-DNAm discordance pole for L15.
3. PMID 37118425 (Waziry 2023, Nature Aging, DOI 10.1038/s43587-022-00357-y): CALERIE RCT — CR slowed DunedinPACE; did not significantly change GrimAge/PhenoAge; authors defer conclusive geroscience test to disease/mortality. Within-DNAm discordance prior on same arm, not Oh organ-age H2H.
4. PMID 38057571 (Oh 2023, Nature, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06802-1): Plasma proteomic organ ages (11 organs) track health/disease; organ age confers mortality and organ-specific risk. Brain/immune referee construct; does not report DunedinPACE/GrimAge co-panel.
Optional: PMID 40634782 (Oh 2025, UKB-scale brain+immune enrichment) — strengthens referee construct but does not co-index DunedinPACE/GrimAge.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. L1–L14 do not prove L15 — L4 asked clock Δ without VO₂/muscle/organ-age as insufficient endpoint; L4 soft-complete DunedinPACE/GrimAge ∩ organ-age = 0 is prior emptiness, not matched H2H adjudication; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated prediction-failure.
2. CALERIE discordance ≠ organ-age prediction failure — PMID 37118425 shows DunedinPACE− / GrimAge flat but does not measure Oh brain+immune organ-age Δ on the same arm.
3. Construct mismatch + adjacent non-matches — blood DNAm ≠ plasma proteomic organ-of-origin; DunedinPACE×MRI brain structure (e.g. PMID 38301452) ≠ Oh proteomic organ-age; reviews ≠ anchors; L4 ≠ L15; no dosing.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis / Critical Dependencies
content_blocks.content:
Three critical ablations identified:
1. Remove CALERIE phase-2 CR-arm H2H stratification of DunedinPACE improvers by GrimAge co-movement with Oh brain+immune organ-age Δ: Without multi-clock × Oh organ-age residual readout, solo-clock LITERATURE and CALERIE within-DNAm discordance cannot show DunedinPACE− without GrimAge fails the organ-age referee.
2. Remove Oh plasma proteomic brain+immune organ-age as adjudication referee: Without the Oh proteomic referee, the card collapses into L4-style clock-without-function or DunedinPACE×MRI adjacent framing and loses the within-DNAm×organ-age H2H.
3. Remove L4≠this + CALERIE-discordance≠organ-age-failure + soft-complete-empty≠failure + MRI≠Oh-proteomic + L1–L14≠proof discipline: Treating L4, CALERIE within-DNAm discordance, empty PubMed, or MRI brain-structure hits as already deciding multi-clock×Oh prediction-failure would invent an H2H result left UNKNOWN.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria and IP/Execution Metadata
content_blocks.content:
Refute if: On the pre-registered CALERIE phase-2 CR-arm multi-clock × Oh organ-age panel, DunedinPACE improvers with GrimAge inside the flat band show Δ organ-age_brain and/or Δ organ-age_immune outside the pre-registered null-benefit band (DunedinPACE− without GrimAge DOES predict Oh brain+immune organ-age benefit / pace-alone suffices on the referee) when sample and assay-definition artifacts are ruled out.

key_findings: L15 is a TRL 1 hypothesis/proposal (NOT_RUN); no new experimental data have been generated.
Central prediction (NEGATIVE polarity): DunedinPACE slowing without concurrent GrimAge improvement fails to predict Oh plasma proteomic brain+immune organ-age benefit on the CALERIE phase-2 CR arm.

CALERIE RCT (PMID 37118425, Waziry 2023) already demonstrates within-DNAm discordance: CR slowed DunedinPACE but did not significantly change GrimAge/PhenoAge — this is the empirical prior, but Oh organ-age was NOT measured on the same arm.
The matched multi-clock × Oh organ-age H2H panel (DunedinPACE∩GrimAge∩Oh brain+immune organ-age) is classified as UNKNOWN — soft-complete search found zero co-indexed studies.

Oh 2023 (PMID 38057571) established plasma proteomic organ ages (11 organs) tracking health/disease and mortality, but does not report DunedinPACE/GrimAge co-panel — the referee construct exists but has not been applied to CALERIE.
Key construct distinction: DunedinPACE and GrimAge are blood DNAm-based; Oh organ ages are plasma proteomic organ-of-origin models — fundamentally different measurement modalities.
Proposed method is secondary analysis of existing public trial arm (CALERIE phase-2), not new wet assay or animal/human dosing — estimated kill cost tier 1, time to refute ~4 weeks.
Adjacent DunedinPACE×MRI brain-structure associations (e.g. PMID 38301452) are explicitly noted as NOT equivalent to Oh proteomic organ-age adjudication.
Competing outcome pre-registered: pace-alone-suffices / missing-Oh-measures / underpowered-strata / construct-mismatch artifact are allowed as inconclusive (not refutation) outcomes.
FTO status: UNKNOWN; IP class: multi-clock-discordance; vault_hold: no.
